description:
Leadership is not the thing we do. It’s what the room becomes when we do it.

In this talk, conductor, educator, and embodied leadership researcher Cory Boulton makes the case that the most urgent problem in leadership isn’t a people problem, but a readiness problem: one that lives entirely with the leader.

Drawing on neuroscience, twenty-five years on the podium, and one unforgettable student, Boulton reframes what it means to be ready. Because those in your charge aren’t just watching you…they are becoming you.

In an era where AI can out-execute us on every technical layer, the most powerful thing a human being brings to their people isn’t what they know, but who they are. Dr. Cory Boulton is a musician, conductor, and educator whose life's work sits at the intersection of presence, leadership, and sound. title: Leadership is not what you do—here’s why | Cory Boulton | TEDxBradley University

What if the thing people celebrate you for isn't the thing you truly want to pursue?

At nine years old, Ganta Jishnu Aryan has already achieved a Guinness World Records title by recalling 216 decimal places of the Golden Ratio. But in this TEDx talk, he asks us to look beyond the record, the praise and other people's expectations — and discover the direction that comes from within.

For Jishnu, that direction is football. Through stories of scraped knees, losing matches, facing fear and continuing to return to the field, he shares a simple idea: knowing where you are going matters more than knowing where everyone else expects you to go.

His message is for anyone who has ever felt defined by an achievement, a label, or someone else's expectations. Ganta Jishnu Aaryan is a 10-year-old Guinness World Records title holder and an aspiring footballer who believes that age is never a barrier to extraordinary achievement.

Her speech asks one to put aside their preconceived notions about an individual and to ask himself whether making an error to shape the rest of his existence is an honest means of determining his character?

A class in the prison was the source for powerful insights into the transforming possibilities of education, empathy and opportunity to begin again, as Eleena reflects. She calls attention to the importance of offering second chances, not as a do-over but as a chance to learn and grow and rebuild.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What can riding a motorcycle through some of the world’s most challenging terrain teach us about facing the unexpected?
Travel film producer Theodosis Dallas shares stories from motorcycle expeditions across Morocco, the Himalayas and the Amazon, where accidents, extreme weather and disrupted plans repeatedly forced him and his team to adapt. Through these experiences, he discovered a lesson that extends far beyond riding: when an obstacle appears, freezing can make it harder to overcome, while staying in motion can help reveal a way through.
But moving does not always mean moving forward. Sometimes it means changing direction, improvising or letting go of the original plan altogether. For Theodosis, resilience is not about having everything under control. It is about continuing to respond, adapt and move because, on a motorcycle and in life, balance is often found in motion.
